subject: Access Fence & Key Custody: Proposal for Ephemeral Operator Keys and Transfer Log Minimization
messages:
From: Claire Huang <claire@betahealth.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: BetaHealth Security <security@betahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 27 May 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Private deploy questions: operator access and key custody

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the demo last week — the private deployment looks promising. Before we proceed to procurement we have three specific asks from InfoSec and Legal: 

1) Who holds the customer master key (CMK) in a VPC/on‑prem scenario? We need to understand if Redwood ever has a key that can decrypt customer data.
2) Can operator actions (breakglass, rotation, emergency access) be made ephemeral and fully logged without retaining plaintext transfer logs?
3) Cross‑border routing: if part of the control plane is in another region for redundancy, what data (if any) crosses jurisdictions?

I've attached our consolidated questionnaire (betahealth-questions.xlsx).

Can your team propose a narrow set of contractual commitments (an annex to the DPA) that would address these? Ideally we want minimal operator footprint and a clear escrow/escrow‑release pattern.

Best,
Claire
Claire Huang
Security Program Manager, BetaHealth
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
To: Claire Huang <claire@betahealth.com>
Cc: BetaHealth Security <security@betahealth.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 27 May 2025 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy questions: operator access and key custody

Claire — thanks for the clear list. I circulated your questionnaire to Product Security and the Deploy team and sketched a focused approach (attached: access-fence-proposal.pdf) we think would meet BetaHealth's requirements without heavy operational overhead. High level: 

- BYOK model by default: customer supplies CMK and Redwood never stores an unencrypted copy. We support KMS integrations (customer KMS or HSM appliance) and an escrow option only on explicit, contractually limited request.
- Ephemeral operator keys: operator actions that require elevated access are performed using short‑lived ephemeral service keys derived by a split‑knowledge protocol — operator control plane never holds long‑term decrypt capability.
- Tokenized operator workflows: where possible, we tokenise requests so that operator telemetry and call traces use token references, not plaintext data. Detailed audit events are retained but redact sensitive payloads.
- Transfer minimization: control plane pings and health metrics are aggregated at a metadata level and routed within the specified region unless you permit cross‑region failover. We can add a clause limiting cross‑border control messages to only encrypted heartbeats and masked metrics.

Next steps I propose: 1) Internal tech note from Marcus on the ephemeral key design; 2) Draft DPA annex redline for Legal review; 3) 30‑minute call early next week to walk the BetaHealth team through the design and signatures.

I've CC'd Lauren from Legal to start the annex work.

Attachments: access-fence-proposal.pdf

—
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com, Claire Huang <claire@betahealth.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 27 May 2025 13:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy questions: operator access and key custody

Claire / Jasmine — quick technical clarifications from Infra & Security (Marcus here added a couple of implementation constraints in line):

- Ephemeral operator keys: we use an HSM‑backed key‑wrap where the CMK (customer) never leaves the customer's KMS in plaintext. For operator tasks that require unwrapping, we require multi‑party attestation: (a) customer service account signs an approval token, (b) Redwood operator identity performs the job using a one‑time key issued by an internal ephemeral CA. The CA keys are short‑lived (15min) and logged.
- Audit logs: we can separate two audit streams — (1) operator activity (who/when/action) with redacted payload hashes, (2) forensic logs available only under MAU (mutual agreement/escrow) with a tracked release workflow and documentable legal trigger. The default retention for full forensic logs is 0 days (not stored) unless escrow is agreed in DPA annex.
- Cross‑region control plane: redundancy nodes exchange encrypted heartbeat tokens only. No model inputs, full payloads, or unencrypted metadata leave the provisioned region. Failover triggers can be configured to stay intra‑region for BetaHealth.

Marcus — any concerns on performance for decrypt‑on‑demand for short jobs?

—
Irene Choi
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
To: Claire Huang <claire@betahealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 27 May 2025 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy questions: operator access and key custody

Claire — thanks for the quick review and the questions. Summarizing agreed proposal and action items (for the DPA annex / procurement):

1) Default posture: BYOK (customer KMS) — Redwood does not retain any customer plaintext CMK.
2) Operator access: ephemeral operator keys with split‑approval; operator audit stream kept; forensic payloads only released under documented MAU/escrow process.
3) Audit retention: full forensic logs are not stored by default; we will surface redacted operator activity logs for 180 days. If BetaHealth requests escrowed forensic logs, the DPA annex must specify legal triggers and retention window (we will provide an option, not default).
4) Cross‑border routing: control plane messages remain regional; encrypted heartbeats for failover only and no payload transfer without explicit approval.

Next steps: 
- Lauren will draft the DPA annex redline (dpa-annex-redline.docx) and circulate to BetaHealth Legal.
- Marcus to provide short tech note on ephemeral key lifecycle and expected latency impact (aim <50ms added for typical unwrap).
- Schedule 30m call — propose Mon 2 Jun 2025 10:00 PT. HubSpot deal link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-4391 

Claire, can you confirm: 1) BetaHealth comfortable with default forensic retention = 0 and redacted operator logs = 180 days? 2) Would you like the escrow option included as an opt‑in (with legal triggers enumerated) or excluded entirely from the annex?

Attachments: dpa-annex-redline.docx

Thanks,
Jasmine
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
